title: Finite geometric stalks of prime-coefficient curve direct images
statement: Let f : C → S be a proper smooth morphism of schemes with nonempty geometrically connected fibres of dimension one. For every prime ell, every nonnegative integer q, and every geometric point s : Spec Ω → S with Ω algebraically closed, the geometric stalk of R^q f_* of the constant lifted F_ell-module is a finite set. Direct images, geometric stalks and constructibility use [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] and [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. No invertibility of ell and no Noetherian hypothesis on S is required.

proof.text:
smoothness and geometric connectedness imply geometric irreducibility. The
residue-field dimension hypothesis therefore gives smooth relative dimension one.
After base change to the algebraically closed field, the source is a smooth proper
connected curve of dimension one. The curve calculation C5 gives finite cohomology of
the constant module R/(ell), where R is the lifted prime field. Since ell = 0 in R,
this constant module is R. The module/abelian cohomology comparison and the Ext/derived
comparison transfer C5 to module-valued derived cohomology. Proper base change identifies
the required stalk with this cohomology; inverse image preserves the constant sheaf.
The input constant sheaf has finite stalks by the constant-stalk isomorphism, supplying
the finiteness hypothesis of the geometric-fibre formula.

theorem prime_constant_stalk_finite
    {C S : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ S) [Smooth f] [IsProper f]
    [GeometricallyConnected f]
    (hdim : ∀ s : S, topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber s) = 1)
    (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (q : ℕ)
    (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) :
    Finite (((Scheme.pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber
      (A := ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ell)))).obj
      (higherDirectImage (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ell)) f q
        ((constantSheaf C.smallEtaleTopology _).obj
          (ModuleCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ell)) (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ell))))))
